title: Adsorption Mechanisms and AI-Driven Discovery of Biomass-Based CO2 Sorbents

metadata.authors: F. Hajiali; J. Chen; T. Zou; S. Renneckar; B. Gopaluni; N. Ellis; O. J. Rojas

source_summary: This review analyzes recent advances in biomass-derived activated carbon for carbon capture, highlighting the impact of precursor selection, treatments, functional groups, and AI-driven technologies on adsorption performance and emphasizing the need for further research to improve scalability and cost-effectiveness of bio-based solutions.
abstract: The pressing need to reduce carbon dioxide emissions has driven recent advances in carbon capture technologies. Among these, adsorption has emerged as one of the most efficient and promising methods for CO<inf>2</inf> sequestration. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of recent progress in biomass-derived activated carbon (AC) as a sustainable solution for carbon capture. It explores the influence of various biomass precursors, their composition, and the effects of chemical and thermal treatments on the textural properties and CO<inf>2</inf> adsorption capacity of AC. The role of functional groups and pore structures in enhancing adsorption performance, particularly under humid conditions, is also examined. Additionally, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven technologies in process modeling and the discovery of optimized bio-based AC materials is highlighted. Classic adsorption kinetic models are reviewed to provide deeper insights into CO<inf>2</inf> adsorption mechanisms and the efficiency of bio-based AC. The discussion underscores the necessity of continued research to enhance the properties, scalability, and cost-effectiveness of bio-based AC while leveraging AI-driven innovations to advance carbon capture and storage (CCS) solutions. © 2025 The Author(s).
